audit_findings.title: Debt-funded cash is counted as equity value while the 0% notes' cash claim is absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $805.0 million, equal to 45.0% of the $1,788.0 million base equity value and $29.02 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds note proceeds held as cash, while equity-level OE contains no recurring interest charge for the 0% notes and the bridge does not recognize their cash-settled principal.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will satisfy its conversion obligations by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of notes to be converted, and by issuing shares of its Class A Common Stock or a combination of cash and shares of its Class A Common Stock, at its election for the incremental value.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator error. Issuing the notes increased bridge cash without an offsetting economic claim, even though the filed settlement terms require cash payment up to principal. The $805.0 million claim is large enough to materially change intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Rerun all scenarios after either deducting the $805.0 million cash-settled principal, excluding the corresponding debt-funded cash from excess cash, or explicitly modeling repayment or refinancing cash flows without double counting.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge treats expansion funding as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: More than $560.0 million of announced Oak Ridge investment, equal to more than 31.3% of base equity value and more than $20.19 per valuation share; other expansion funding and net DOE reimbursement effects are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash reserved for manufacturing and enrichment expansion is included in the bridge as distributable cash, while the simple OE growth path does not model the associated investment outflows or resulting operating cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to increase our capital expenditures by approximately several hundred million, driven by ongoing investments and a strategic shift towards our manufacturing readiness plan and Ohio expansion.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification of all $1.8685 billion as excess cash is unsupported by the filed spending plans. The precise adjustment remains unresolved because DOE milestone funding, project timing, minimum liquidity, and committed spending are not reconciled, but the filed investment scale is plainly material.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 30, 2026 cash-perimeter schedule separating minimum operating liquidity, authorized Oak Ridge and Piketon expenditures, escrowed or committed amounts, DOE-funded or reimbursable costs, and genuinely distributable cash; then rerun the bridge and operating forecast consistently.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted denominator does not match the convertibles' cash-principal settlement
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed overstatement of approximately 5.821 million shares: 7.634 million full-conversion shares versus approximately 1.814 million incremental shares at $173.89; an unchanged-numerator base value would be approximately $81.56 rather than $64.47
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator includes shares for conversion principal that must instead be paid in cash; only conversion value above principal can produce incremental shares.
audit_findings.evidence: However, because the principal amount of the 2.25% Convertible Notes and 0% Convertible Notes must be settled in cash, the dilutive impact of applying the if-converted method is limited to the in-the-money portion, if any, of the 2.25% Convertible Notes and 0% Convertible Notes.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated denominator error. At $173.89, the 0% notes are below their approximately $229.62 conversion price and contribute no incremental shares, while the 2.25% notes contribute only their in-the-money conversion value. The approximately 26.5% denominator overstatement materially affects per-share value, although a consistent rerun must also recognize the notes' cash claims.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate price-dependent incremental shares for each convertible at every scenario value, retain other equity awards separately, incorporate cash-settled principal consistently in the numerator, and rerun value per share and buy-below thresholds.

audit_findings.title: Material unfunded retiree benefits may be an unbridged senior economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $81.4 million obligation, equal to 4.6% of base equity value and $2.93 per valuation share; $9.2 million expected 2026 payment
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion not already captured through OE cash outflows would reduce excess cash or require explicit runoff payments in the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has material unfunded postretirement health and life benefit obligations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated error because the record does not show whether OE already captures benefit payments. Even deducting the entire filed obligation would reduce base value only from $64.47 to approximately $61.54 per share and would not alter the conclusion relative to the $173.89 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace actual and projected retiree-benefit cash payments through the OE calculation; if they are absent, model the disclosed runoff or deduct the residual obligation, but do not do both.

audit_findings.title: TENEX creates an off-balance-sheet take-or-pay exposure
audit_findings.mechanism: Mandatory purchases could reduce future OE through payments for unusable or unprofitable SWU, stranded inventory, replacement supply costs, or losses on matching customer contracts.
audit_findings.evidence: The TENEX Supply Contract provides that the Company must pay for all SWU in its minimum purchase obligation each year, even if it fails to submit orders for such SWU.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved existing contractual exposure, not merely a hypothetical risk: the filing confirms annual minimum-purchase and payment obligations through a contract that may extend to 2028. Confidential quantities, prices, committed sales, waivers, and mitigation prevent the record from establishing its valuation magnitude.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the remaining annual minimum quantities and formula prices, match them to firm customer sales and applicable licenses or waivers, calculate stranded or replacement-cost downside cases, and rerun OE under those cases.

audit_findings.title: Customer advances embedded in cash are not freely distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: $51.8 million net contract liability at June 30, 2026, computed as $85.0 million deferred revenue less $33.2 million deferred costs; 2.9% of base equity value and $1.87 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Advance-funded cash may require future delivery spending and working-capital reversal; any amount not captured in forecast OE should reduce excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: The LEU segment backlog also includes approximately $0.1 billion of deferred revenue and advances from customers as of December 31, 2025, whereby customers have made advance payments to be applied against future deliveries.
audit_findings.explanation: The advance and related delivery obligation are demonstrated, but double counting is unresolved because future fulfillment effects may already enter OE. Charging the entire latest net contract liability would reduce base value only to approximately $62.60 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $173.89 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30 advances to deferred costs, customer-owned or owed inventory, expected fulfillment margins, and OE working-capital treatment; adjust only the portion not already represented in forecast cash flows.
